name: Short-range cord forager (dense, slow)
description: Grows out of wood as a dense, slowly advancing fan and only consolidates short cords behind it. It finds small, close resources, holds its ground and ranks high in combat.

tip_speed.note: middle of the 1 to 3 mm/day front speed given for short-range cord foragers (research/02 section 4), 2 mm/day; the measured rates for Hypholoma fasciculare are in papers that were not opened (research/08 [14][15])

growth_unit.note: no measurement found; set short because the family is described as having a high branching rate (research/02 section 4)

branch_angle_sd.note: default from Hopkins & Boswell 2012 (79 +/- 10 deg, research/09); not measured for this family

sensitivity.note: how strongly tips turn away from crowding; model coefficient

fusion_probability.note: fitted so that the engine gives about 1 fusion per 8 branches, as measured in Podospora anserina (research/01 [8]); not measured for this species

density_cap.note: hyphal density at which branching stops; tuning value for dense fans

cord_max.note: largest cord cross-section, in single hyphae; cords form late and stay short (research/02 section 4); tuning value

explore.note: willingness to grow over bare soil; lower than the long-range foragers; tuning value

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / 100 so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

inactivation_rate.note: set low because pruning is described as slow and weak (research/02 section 4); no measurement found

degradation_rate.note: none seen in 15 h in R. solani; small value so dead hyphae clear

passive_transport.note: diffusion between neighbouring segments; measured diffusion inside hyphae (1 to 2 x 10^-9 m2/s, research/10) is several times faster than the passes allow

soil.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from the family's ecology, not measured

wood.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from the family's ecology, not measured

litter.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from the family's ecology, not measured

root.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from the family's ecology, not measured

agar.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from the family's ecology, not measured

transport_speed.note: no measurement for this family; near the 14.4 mm/h ceiling for motor transport and the 18 mm/h mass flow measured in Neurospora (research/10)

t_opt.note: extension of Hypholoma fasciculare rises with temperature from 5 to 20 C (research/08 [14]); extension of Stropharia caerulea is sensitive above 25 C (research/06 [37], genus not certain)

cold_drop.note: the type species fruits in autumn (research/08, unchecked); size of the drop is a guess

wobble.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

avoidance.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

fusion_probability.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

uptake.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

turn.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

spike_interval.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

spike_duration.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

spike_amplitude.note: default; no recording for any member of this family (research/04)

score.note: late secondary cord formers top the hierarchy: Hypholoma fasciculare always replaced primary colonisers and Bjerkandera adusta, deadlocked with Trametes versicolor, and was itself replaced by Phanerochaete velutina (research/06 section 2.5 [4])
